LOCAL PYTHON + PINNED NATIVE ENGINE

Run the local workbench.

The source repository and public release tag are being prepared. No public repository or downloadable application binary is claimed on this preview. The recorded example is available now.

SolderShape runs locally. This website does not execute the solver or accept PCB uploads. You need Python 3.12 or newer, a C compiler, make and a modern browser. The application uses Python's standard library. The first setup downloads two hash-pinned upstream archives and builds Surface Evolver.

Start from the source directory

python3 tools/setup_engine.py
python3 -m soldershape serve --port 8765

Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/board. The setup reports ready and the application header identifies the native engine. On macOS, the source also contains a double-click launcher. Apple Silicon macOS with Python 3.14 and Apple clang 21 is the exercised platform. Other platforms remain unqualified.

Reproduce the Board comparison

  1. Select component U1 and pad J16.
  2. Set upper diameter 400 µm, held gap 300 µm and X offset 240 µm.
  3. Set reference liquid volume 40 nL and candidate liquid volume 56 nL.
  4. Use surface tension 0.48 N/m, density 9 g/cm³ and gravity enabled for this hypothetical example.
  5. Compute the selected comparison. Inspect the selected result and save its HTML and Board evidence.

The reference predicts X/Z forces of −184.526/−181.284 µN. The candidate predicts −164.385/+13.386 µN. Less solder meets this declared held-gap fixture objective. This does not select a production solder volume.

Replay the recorded evidence

Download the recorded example and extract the outer package. Keep its notices. From a SolderShape source checkout with the pinned engine installed, run the inner archive.

python3 tools/verify_board.py /path/to/board-comparison.zip --replay

Passing replay establishes numerical agreement within the declared checks. The outer package's README identifies the unchanged inner archive and its exact hash. Read the physical and numerical limits before interpreting the result.
